item.title: Standardised multi-sensor geolocator data for bird migration ecology
item.description:
Raphaël Nussbaumer, Peter Adamík, Fraser Bell, Than Boves, Martins Briedis, Malcolm D. Burgess, Violeta Caballero-Lopez, Pablo Capilla-Lasheras, et al.
Scientific Data
DOI: 10.1038/s41597-026-08873-x
Abstract Multi-sensor geolocators using pressure-based geolocation are becoming increasingly widespread, generating a rapidly growing volume of movement data for birds, covering multiple species, geographic regions, and years. However, differences in data formats, metadata conventions, device types and manufacturers, as well as analysis workflows, currently limit data reuse and cross-study synthesis. Here, we present the GeoLocator Data Package (DP), a standardized framework to publish, curate and combine multi-sensor geolocator data within and across projects. The framework provides a unified and reproducible analysis workflow that enables individual studies using pressure-based geolocators to publish project-specific data packages following a shared structure. These packages can then be aggregated into a single dataset while preserving provenance and attribution. The framework builds on established pressure-based geolocation methods and supports consistent generation of biologically interpretable movement trajectories from multi-sensor data. By following FAIR data principles with documented tools for contributors and users, the GeoLocator DP facilitates reuse of geolocator data for comparative and macro-ecological studies of bird movement.

item.title: A global collection of wind direction-weighted topographic exposure indices (TOPEX) and topographic position indices (TPI) for non-polar land areas
item.description:
Christopher Jung, Kerstin Stahl, Dirk Schindler
Scientific Data, vol. 13, issue 1
DOI: 10.1038/s41597-026-08788-7
Abstract Topographic derivatives are widely used in applied geosciences, yet most metrics describe terrain geometry without capturing directional terrain–atmosphere interactions. We present GloTopIx, a global 250 m × 250 m data collection including anisotropic, wind direction-frequency-weighted topographic exposure ( TOPEX ) and topographic position ( TPI ) indices, together with unweighted base products derived from a harmonized digital elevation model and ERA5-derived wind climatology for 1996–2025. For each grid cell, TOPEX and TPI were computed in eight directions at four search distances (1, 5, 10, and 25 km) to capture multiscale terrain structure. The weighted variants incorporate ERA5 wind direction frequencies at 10 and 100 m, as well as 10 m frequencies under extreme wind conditions. The collection comprises 32 product variants for each of 11 non-polar regional units. Potential applications include meteorological downscaling, geomorphological landform analysis, ecological and forestry studies, hydrological and soil-moisture modeling, fire-risk assessment, and wind turbine siting. Station-based empirical assessment was restricted to Germany. Users should therefore assess the region-specific terrain–climate relationships before applying them in other regions.
